actions.justification: Mandatory first-step action to determine if patient has active bleeding, which guides urgency and transfusion strategy.
Mandatory assessment to evaluate hemodynamic stability, which determines transfusion threshold and urgency (restrictive vs liberal vs massive transfusion protocol).
Mandatory lab to determine hemoglobin/hematocrit level to guide transfusion threshold decision-making.
Mandatory action: Type and screen is required before any blood product administration to ensure compatibility and patient safety.
Mandatory action: Reviewing transfusion history identifies prior reactions, alloantibodies, and guides safe transfusion management.

Optional but clinically indicated: Assessing symptoms of anemia (fatigue, dyspnea, chest pain, dizziness) will help determine appropriate transfusion threshold (restrictive vs. liberal) once CBC results are reviewed.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80, SpO2 98%) with no active bleeding signs. A restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb <7-8 g/dL) is appropriate for stable patients per evidence-based transfusion guidelines, minimizing unnecessary transfusion risks.
Pre-medication with acetaminophen is a standard prophylactic measure to reduce febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions if transfusion is anticipated, given the completed type and screen.
Pre-medication with diphenhydramine is recommended prophylactically prior to transfusion to reduce the risk of allergic transfusion reactions, particularly given reviewed transfusion history.
Ensure reliable IV access is maintained while awaiting CBC results and in case transfusion or other IV therapies are needed.
Normothermia maintenance is important in transfusion patients to prevent hypothermia-related coagulopathy and improve outcomes.
Patient is stable but requires ongoing serial vital sign monitoring every 15 minutes to detect any hemodynamic changes while CBC and type & screen results are pending.
Coagulation status should be monitored as part of the transfusion workup to guide further management and detect any coagulopathy before potential transfusion.
While awaiting CBC results, assess and prepare to apply liberal transfusion threshold (Hb 8 g/dL) if indicated based on patient's clinical context and symptoms of anemia already assessed.
Reticulocyte count helps assess bone marrow response and classify anemia etiology (hemolytic vs. hypoproliferative), guiding further management decisions.
Iron studies (serum iron, ferritin, TIBC) help evaluate for iron deficiency anemia, which is a common and treatable cause of anemia requiring specific management.
Direct antiglobulin test (DAT) is indicated to evaluate for autoimmune hemolytic anemia, especially important in the context of transfusion history to detect alloimmunization or hemolytic reactions.

Patient is at 85 minutes since arrival with labs still pending. Serial reassessment of hemodynamic status is critical to detect any deterioration and guide transfusion decisions while awaiting CBC results.
With CBC pending, reassessing hemoglobin trend is essential to determine if transfusion threshold criteria are met and to guide further management.

TEG provides comprehensive coagulation assessment including clot formation, strength, and fibrinolysis — useful for guiding targeted blood product administration and assessing need for tranexamic acid or other hemostatic agents.
Blood bank workup is needed to process type and screen results and prepare for potential transfusion. Labs are still pending and this ensures blood products can be made available promptly.

Patient has had CBC ordered and reassessment of hemoglobin completed. Once results return, transfusion should be administered if Hb is below 8 g/dL per the liberal threshold already applied in this scenario context.

If active bleeding is present or suspected, tranexamic acid (TXA) should be considered early to reduce fibrinolysis and blood product requirements, consistent with evidence-based transfusion management guidelines.

CBC is pending; if hemoglobin returns below 7 g/dL, transfusion is indicated per restrictive threshold strategy already applied. This conditional order prepares for prompt action once results are available.
